subject: Proposal: move from monthly to yearly reserve with staged performance holdbacks
messages:
From: Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@acme-ai.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing question — switching our account to yearly reserve

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. We’ve been running Redwood on the monthly plan for the last 9 months and we’re ready to move to a yearly/reserve model to get better predictability. A couple of asks from our side so we can put this through procurement: 

- Can you outline the discount tiers for a 1yr vs 2yr reserve? We’re considering both but want to understand effective economics given staged ramp.
- We plan a staged ramp (Q1 light, Q2 medium, Q3 full scale). Can you propose a ramp schedule and any holdbacks or performance-based credits tied to latency/SLOs?
- Procurement needs to know whether we can do a usage true-up during the term (quarterly or annual) and how refunds/credits would be handled.
- Any onboarding fees or migration windows we should budget for?

I attached our procurement request PDF with their intake questions. We’d like a short proposal by end of next week; can you send a sample SOW and a term sheet?

Best,
Sofia Lopez
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme AI

Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing question — switching our account to yearly reserve

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear brief and the procurement PDF. High-level framework below; I’ve attached a working term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-v1.xlsx) you can share with procurement.

TL;DR proposal (first pass)
- Term: 12-month prepaid reserve billed up front. Option to extend to 24 months for an incremental effective discount.
- Pricing approach: tiered effective discounts based on committed USD spend and multi-year commitment. For example (illustrative): 12mo reserve -> blended ~17-20% discount vs current monthly rates; 24mo reserve -> additional 4-6% reduction (final numbers after usage profile review).
- Staged ramp (recommended): 3 tranches (onboarding -> scale -> steady-state). We propose a 40/35/25 expected usage split across months 1–4 / months 5–8 / months 9–12 respectively, with a built-in smoothing credit if actual usage exceeds or undershoots by >15% per tranche.
- Performance holdback: propose 10% of the annual reservation be held as a performance pool tied to SLOs (latency P99, availability). Missed SLOs generate credits back to Acme; over-delivery (sustained better latency) would reduce holdback release thresholds.
- True-ups: annual true-up by default; can accommodate quarterly true-ups operationally but that changes billing flow and requires approvals from finance/legal.
- Migration/onboarding: we can waive the one-time migration fee if the commitment meets the minimum threshold; onboarding timeline typically 4–6 weeks for the transition.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Marissa for pricing approvals and Karthik for ops/finance constraints. If this sounds reasonable, we’ll produce a short SOW + DocuSign-ready term summary.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pricing question — switching our account to yearly reserve

Looping in ops and finance. Naomi — solid structure. A few commercial points to align internally before we finalize language to Acme procurement: 

- Need finance sign-off on whether we can do upfront billing for full year vs staged invoice for first year. If finance requires staged invoices we should propose a short pro-rata upfront + annual remainder (ops prefers a single invoice for cashflow reasons).
- Legal will want to limit exposure on the holdback; propose maximum liability equal to the held amount (i.e., 10% pool) and explicit SLO measurement windows.
- Recommend offering a one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) rather than reducing list discount — cleaner for renewals. Suggested credit: $25k if they commit >= $500k ARR equivalent.
- Ask: confirm whether Acme needs net-30 or net-60 payment terms; procurement sometimes asks for 60.

I’ll prepare the billing-migration-checklist and a short note for legal. Ben — can you backfill any client-specific concessions we’ve given historically for similar-sized accounts? Karthik — ops constraints?

—Marissa
Senior Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

Operational notes from ops/finance perspective: 

- Billing model: We can support (A) full upfront annual invoice, (B) 3x tranche invoice (first tranche upfront pro-rated, then two subsequent invoices at month 4 and month 8), or (C) annual invoice with quarterly usage true-ups. Each option has different accounting treatments (revenue recognition). Finance prefers option A for revenue certainty.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups are operationally heavier but doable; annual true-up is standard. If Acme insists on quarterly true-ups, there will be a small admin fee to cover processing.
- Holdback administration: we need a clear SLO measurement doc and a retained credit ledger. Ops needs a signed acceptance of SLO definitions before we lock the pool.
- Region/regulatory: confirm that billing will be USD and regional support remains US; any EU or APAC components may require separate clauses.

I’ve dropped a billing-migration-checklist in the thread for Marissa/legal to refine. HubSpot link to the account record in case you want to attach the terms: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME-98765

-Karthik
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Michael / Sofia — summarizing agreed commercial direction and proposed next steps to get procurement to signature. This is intended to be client-facing language we can drop into a short proposal.

Proposed commercial summary (final draft)
- Term & Billing: 12-month prepaid reserve billed upfront (option to elect 24 months at signature). Billing in USD; Net-30 standard (Net-60 can be offered with PO).
- Pricing / Discount: Effective ~18% blended discount off monthly list rates for the 12-month reserve (finalized after we ingest the last 6 months of usage). 24-month option receives an additional 4% effective reduction.
- Ramp & Overages: Staged ramp with expected split 40% / 35% / 25% across onboarding / scale / steady-state. If monthly consumption exceeds the committed tranche by >25%, overage will be billed at the committed rate for the remainder of the tranche; sustained overage across a full month triggers a true-up at the pay-as-you-go rate for the excess usage.
- Holdback & Credits: 10% of the invoice amount reserved in a performance pool. Any missed SLOs (pre-agreed P99 latency windows or monthly availability thresholds) convert to credits applied to the next invoice. Holdback release schedule: 50% released at month 6 if SLOs are met; remainder released at month 12. Redwood liability limited to the held pool amount.
- True-ups: Annual true-up by default; quarterly true-ups available with a small admin fee.
- Onboarding & Credits: Redwood will waive the standard migration fee and provide a one-time $25k onboarding credit if Acme signs >= $500k commitment.
- Deliverables: Short SOW (attached: SOW_draft.pdf) + DocuSign packet to follow.

Next actions (owners):
- Legal/Finance (Redwood): finalize DocuSign-ready term summary and legal exhibit (Marissa / Karthik) — target 2026-07-24.
- Redwood (Naomi): send Draft SOW and prefill DocuSign envelope — target 2026-07-21 (attached).
- Acme: confirm payment terms (Net-30 vs Net-60) and final ramp percentages by 2026-07-23.

If this matches Acme’s expectations I’ll ask our legal team to convert to DocuSign and we’ll route for signature.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
